what_this_is: The record of an end-to-end reproduction of the two committed Terraform plan artefacts from a genuinely fresh `git clone` of github.com/Shaugato/mainline, taken on 2026-08-14 by worker W4 of the docs-and-deploy wave. Every command, exit code and count below was captured from the process's own exit status, never from the tail of a pipeline. NO `terraform apply` WAS RUN. plan_repro.sh's refusal allowlist and its stage-2 empty-state equivalence check were not weakened; a stage-2b build-input check and exit code 10 were ADDED, and both are exercised below.

hazard_1_core_longpaths.claim: On Windows with `core.longpaths` unset, `git clone` of this repository into a long parent directory produces a PARTIAL checkout. The reviewer is left with a tree that still contains all of `infra/`, `scripts/deploy/`, `evidence/deploy/` and `docs/deploy/` — so `terraform init -backend=false` and `terraform validate` both SUCCEED against something that is not this repository.

attempt_A_long_parent_no_longpaths.why_this_is_dangerous_even_at_exit_128: The message a human reads begins `Clone succeeded`. The directory exists, the branch is checked out, and every path a Terraform reviewer needs is present. A shell that chains with `&&` stops; a human, or a `;`-separated recipe, does not.

detector.reading_note: The aborted checkout also left the INDEX empty, which is why every one of the 7,548 HEAD files shows as `D ` even though 1,131 of them are on disk. The row count is therefore a DETECTOR, not a file census — it over-reports. The census is `git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only` diffed against the filesystem, and it says 6,417. Both numbers are recorded here rather than one, because a runbook that hands a reviewer a number they cannot reproduce is the defect this wave exists to remove.
detector.requirement: `git status --short` MUST be empty immediately after a clone. Anything else means the checkout is incomplete.

attempt_B_same_long_parent_with_longpath.verdict: `core.longpaths=true` is a complete remedy at this path length. The hazard is a configuration default, not a repository defect.

hazard_2_autocrlf.claim: This repository carries NO `.gitattributes`. Git for Windows sets `core.autocrlf=true` in a fresh clone's local config, so a fresh Windows clone's `.tf` files are CRLF while the tree the committed artefacts were generated from is LF. `terraform show -json` embeds a variable's `description` heredoc verbatim, so every newline inside it becomes `\r\n` in the JSON — and the regenerated JSON artefact is 4,588 bytes larger with 125 differing `description` values, none of which is a change of meaning.

measured.second_order_effect: In the CRLF clone `module.guard[0].data.archive_file.responder` also came back with a different id (57394f85… -> b99493da…) and a different `source_code_hash`, because `archive_file` zips the responder's own source and CRLF changes those bytes. In the LF clone the responder's id and hash reproduce EXACTLY.

hazard_2_autocrlf.remedy: Clone with `git -c core.autocrlf=false clone …` when the point of the clone is to regenerate or byte-compare an artefact.
hazard_2_autocrlf.reported_to_lead_not_actioned: A committed `.gitattributes` pinning `*.tf text eol=lf` would remove this class of difference for every future reviewer. `.gitattributes` is not a file W4 owns, so this is a recommendation, not a change.

Rebuilding it inside the clone needs `verticals/mainline/apps/console/dist/`, which needs a 305 MB `node_modules` and a pnpm/vite build; that chain was out of this run's reach and is recorded as an honest limit rather than glossed. THE PACKAGE'S BYTES REACH THE PLAN AS EXACTLY ONE VALUE — `source_code_hash` — and do not touch the resource count, which is why the counts below are trustworthy while the artefact bytes are not byte-identical.
package_supplied_for_this_run.known_impurity: That zip was built from the workstation's working tree, which at the time of this run carried four other workers' uncommitted edits under verticals/mainline/apps/demo-api/. It is therefore NOT the HEAD package, and its hash differs from the one in the committed artefact. This is the single reason the regenerated artefacts are not byte-identical, and it is also the single reason they were NOT committed over the top.

decision_on_committing_the_regenerated_a.decision: THE FOUR COMMITTED PLAN ARTEFACTS WERE NOT OVERWRITTEN. `git diff` over `evidence/**` for this worker adds this file and changes nothing else.
decision_on_committing_the_regenerated_a.which_side_is_authoritative: The committed plan artefact, per docs/leads/docs-and-cloud-plan.md RULING 4 and docs/deploy/terraform-plan.md §0.1 — the artefact is authoritative and the prose is derived. Nothing was moved to match anything: the artefacts were re-measured and found correct on every claim any document derives from them.
why_not_overwrite: The purpose of regenerating was to test the authoritative count. The count reproduced, four times, in both shapes. A regeneration that confirms the record is a reason to keep the record, not to replace it.

The ONLY substantive difference is `source_code_hash`, and the package it hashes was built from a working tree carrying four other workers' UNCOMMITTED edits. Writing that hash into committed evidence would replace a record of a coherent tree with a record of a tree that exists on one machine for one afternoon. That is strictly worse evidence.

The regeneration environment is a Windows clone. Committing its JSON without `core.autocrlf=false` would rewrite 125 `description` values from LF to CRLF — the exact defect docs/deploy/terraform-plan.md §1 already records and corrected: `All four are LF-terminated, because that is what Terraform writes; two of them previously carried CRLF, which was an artefact of the shell that captured them and not something the tool emitted.`

Every remaining difference — the plan's `timestamp`, the ordering of concurrent data-source reads, the order of `relevant_attributes` — is non-deterministic output of the tool and carries no information. Churning four evidence files, and the §1 SHA-256 table that quotes them, to record noise would make the next real drift harder to see.
decision_on_committing_the_regenerated_a.what_would_change_this: A regeneration from a clone taken with `core.autocrlf=false` whose Lambda package was built inside that clone from HEAD. If such a run returns a count other than 24 / 35 it is an escalation under RULING 7 and not an edit; if it returns the same counts with a different `source_code_hash`, the artefacts should be replaced as a set, in one commit, together with the §1 hash table.
decision_on_committing_the_regenerated_a.what_was_NOT_done: No evidence file was edited so that a document would become true. No document was edited to a new number on this worker's authority. No count, floor, ceiling or known-red list was lowered. No `terraform apply`, no `continue-on-error`, no `|| true`.

still_not_proven_by_this_run: Nothing was applied. Every figure here describes an exposure that does not exist.
The Lambda package was not built inside the clone, so the reproduction is complete for the plan's SHAPE and COUNT and incomplete for its `source_code_hash`.
The console `dist/` build was not exercised at all; the runbook names it as a step on the authority of build_lambda.sh's own header, not of a run.

`terraform plan` was reproduced against a LOCAL backend whose state is empty. plan_repro.sh MEASURES that the remote state is empty on every run and exits 5 when it is not, and it measured it as empty here — but the equivalence expires at the first apply and this run cannot prove anything about the world after one.
